newsitem.title: UK: IGC ups India, China coarse grains, world unchange.
newsitem.headline: IGC ups India, China coarse grains, world unchange.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday left its estimate for 1996 world coarse grains output unchanged from January's figure at 881 million tonnes.
But a global change of just 100,000 tonnes in total production before rounding conceals several country changes.

The IGC raised its estimate for India's crop to 32.3 million tonnes from the previous 30.9 million and put China's output up at 129.8 million tonnes,from 129.3 million previously. But it cut the estimate for South African production to 9.0 million tonnes from the previous 10.3 million.
Indonesia's estimated output was also cut, to 6.6 million tonnes from the previous 7.5 million.
There was also a rise in the Baltic states output, to 3.0 million from the previously estimated 2.7 million.
In aggregate the changes cut world maize production from the previous estimate of 571.3 million tonnes to 568.7 million.

This is largely offset by a rise in the barley estimate, to 155.0 million tonnes from the previous 154.7 million. There is also a rise in estimated rye production to 24.1 million tonnes, from the previous 24.0 million. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom
